g4ela-29-1-morphology: Three more Latin bases. Rupt means break, so to interrupt is to break in. Duct and duce mean lead, so an aqueduct leads water across a valley. Form means shape, so a formation is a shape made by many people. Find the base. It carries the meaning.
g4ela-29-2-grammar: Commas in dates and places. A date: June 12, 1941. The comma sits between the day and the year. A place: Dover, Kent. The comma sits between the town and the bigger place it belongs to. If the sentence keeps going, add one more comma after.
g4ela-29-3-spelling: Long words are built from parts you already know. Find the part, and spell it the same way every time. Portable: port, able. Spectator: spect, a, tor. The part never changes its spelling, even when the word around it does.
g4ela-29-4-grammar: Editing day. Read each date and place. Is there a comma between the day and the year? Between the town and the bigger place? And if the sentence keeps going, is there a comma after? Fix each one and say what it separates.
